title: IncomingSearchV1 — typed INPUT that source universe S searched target universe U at relation@rung (DRAFT)
description: Canonical-record INPUT. Not inferred from producer facts. Not an empty Cartesian Coverage key (S,U). Used only when no CoverageResultV3 exists with key (relation, minResolution, sourceUniverse=S, targetUniverse=U). Cannot override a represented Coverage S->U that is partial/unknown. Identity is raw SHA-256 of C(this record). Uniqueness: (planId, providerClosure, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, minResolution). Standing: isolated successor draft. Root registers the payload-registry / ProofInputRef row. Globally admitted by OWN registered relation/rung; an atom consumes only attestations of its relation@minResolution. ResolutionCompletenessV2 and ClosedWorldV2 are copied exact native owner types (native-evidence.schemas.v2.json); no invented open objects and no default resolved-complete.

providerClosure.description: Plan-selected closure kind=provider that examined S. Not evaluator. Must equal each named scope's enumeratorClosure.

scopeRefs.description: Exact union of THIS providerClosure's owned scopes of the attestation relation at EXACT minResolution whose sourceUniverse is S (enumeratorClosure=providerClosure). Two selected providers on the same U have disjoint owned-scope sets; each attests its own. Not a per-target-subject Cartesian. Program identity remains U.

expectedInventoryRefs.description: Exact union of raw SHA-256 of C(SubjectInventoryV1) locators of THIS provider on S at the source kind. Not a caller-added inventoryDigest field. When inventories carry enumerator locators, refs are that provider's locators only. Partial/unavailable inventories are valid refs; they make population unknown rather than listing fake IDs. Empty expected set is a misjoin, never a skipped check.

completeSearch.description: true: this source's examination considered target U (whole-source-to-target-universe search, not per-subject Cartesian). false: search of U not established. true is refused unless examinedExhaustive is true.

examinedExhaustive.description: false must never prove complete search. coverage=complete and completeSearch=true both require this true (native RC-6 analogue).

x-opensip-law.cartesian: FORBIDDEN. This record attests that source program S searched target universe U as a whole at relation@rung. It does not mint per-target-subject Coverage keys.
x-opensip-law.coverageFirst: If a CoverageResultV3 exists with exact (relation, minResolution, S, U) on THIS provider's owned scopes, that Coverage is the search law for those partitions. Partial/unknown Coverage of THIS provider cannot be overridden by that provider's completeSearch=true. Another provider's partial S->U does not make this attestation structurally invalid; incoming evaluation remains unknown until every owed provider is complete.
x-opensip-law.whenUsed: Only when no such Coverage exists. Then this admitted record may stand in for the missing S->U search. completeSearch=false, coverage=unknown, or examinedExhaustive=false leaves incoming absence unknown. Dependency sufficiency uses actual DEPENDS_ON Coverage of S, never a fictional complete dependency entry.
x-opensip-law.otherPartitions: Coverage/scopes S->V (V≠U) still count toward source-population union and must be sufficiency-accounted per scope. They do not prove search of U. Each source partition needs S->U Coverage or a valid provider-owned whole-source attestation. Provider groups are seeded from selected program contributors, not only emitted scopes.
x-opensip-law.globalAdmit: Admit every attestation against its OWN registered relation and ladder rung, then consume only those matching the current atom. Mixed-atom policies are ordinary.
x-opensip-law.inventoryDigest: expectedInventoryRefs are raw SHA-256 of C(SubjectInventoryV1) computed from the inventory record (schema fields only). Caller-added inventoryDigest is not an authority. Exact set equality with THIS provider's locators of (sourceUniverse, source kind) when enumerator locators exist; otherwise the U union. Missing inventories are a misjoin, never a skipped check.
x-opensip-law.multiProvider: Native enumeration-plan does not forbid two selected provider enumerators on the same U across workspace cells. Uniqueness remains (planId, providerClosure, S, T, relation, minResolution). Each attestation owns that provider's scopes and inventory locators. Program identity U is still one.
joins: providerClosure is Plan-selected, closures[id].kind=provider, and is an enumerator of an available EnumerationPlan binding whose universe=S for capabilityForRelation[att.relation] (one of possibly several on S)
targetUniverse is an admitted selected native universe (portable domain in universeDomains and/or a selected program binding universe); an unattached digest is refused even if unused
relation is registered; minResolution is a member of THAT relation's ladder (not the current atom's relation)

scopeRefs is the exact union of this providerClosure's owned scopes (enumeratorClosure=providerClosure) at relation/resolution/sourceUniverse=S; every named scope must admit under the native subject-scope carrier, including its required nonnull enumeratorClosure; there is no admitted untagged-scope fallback
expectedInventoryRefs is the exact union of raw C digests of this provider's SubjectInventoryV1 locators of universe S at the source kind

resolutionCompleteness/closedWorld validate as native ResolutionCompletenessV2 / ClosedWorldV2 using the native owner AdmissionError class; RC-1 applies (non-resolved rung is not-applicable; resolved rung is never not-applicable); no default resolved-complete
